tools.summary: Explain every available Operations Pulse tool and connection path.
tools.whenToUse: At setup, launch, or whenever an operator asks what the system can do.
tools.example: Show me the available tools and which ones require accounts.

tools.summary: Query the local operational ticket memory.
tools.whenToUse: Before staffing new work or when reviewing the queue.
tools.dataBoundary: Reads the configured local SQLite database.
tools.example: List open high-priority tickets related to authentication.

tools.summary: Add an explicit ticket to the local queue.
tools.whenToUse: When a human or a verified pulse result identifies actionable work.
tools.dataBoundary: Writes one record to local SQLite.
tools.example: Create a medium-priority ticket for the stale onboarding docs.

tools.summary: Run configured operational checks and store their evidence.
tools.whenToUse: On demand or from a scheduler for a heartbeat-style review.
tools.dataBoundary: Reads the chosen workspace and configured local logs; stores pulse evidence locally.
tools.example: Run a read-only pulse against this repository.

tools.summary: Read recent heartbeat outcomes and evidence summaries.
tools.whenToUse: When looking for repeated noise, regressions, or changes over time.
tools.example: Show the last ten pulse runs and failed checks.

tools.summary: Show optional integrations, setup modes, permissions, and cost classes.
tools.whenToUse: Before connecting email, ticketing, observability, or model providers.
tools.dataBoundary: Reads connection metadata; never returns credentials.
tools.example: Which email integrations support bring-your-own credentials?

tools.summary: Read safe local connection state without exposing credentials.
tools.whenToUse: After using the CLI or host connection picker to confirm which adapters are configured and recently tested.
tools.dataBoundary: Reads local connection metadata and environment-variable presence only; never reads or returns credential values.
tools.example: Which Operations Pulse adapters are connected, and which still need a credential?

tools.summary: Read whether the optional local heartbeat schedule is installed.
tools.whenToUse: Before starting, reviewing, or removing a local recurring pulse.
tools.dataBoundary: Reads only the named user-level scheduler file.
tools.example: Is the Operations Pulse heartbeat installed on this machine?
